description: Statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy, app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY and the shipped ASCII fixture, and NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL: executing these programs is empirically impossible in this environment - there is no z/OS and no CICS emulator, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled and refuses a PROCEDURE ... USING program under -x, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters that break parsing, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. That substitutes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else (AAP 0.7.6, practice B12, risk R-A, where the substitution is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than silently absorbed). Every byte below is read out of three places and no fourth: the post-check at app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl:1477-1492, the field offsets of app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy, and rows 0 to 2 of src/test/resources/fixtures/carddata.txt. Nothing here is a measurement of a run and it must never be described as one. THIS IS THE REWRITE-FAILURE CASE, and it exists to pin ONE STATEMENT: the unguarded SET at :1491. THE UNIT IS THE SERVICE, NOT THE CONTROLLER. unitKind is SERVICE: card.CardUpdateService is constructed through its own constructor over a fixture-backed card.CardRepository - readForUpdateByCardNumber for the READ ... UPDATE at :1427-1436 and rewrite for the REWRITE at :1477-1483 - and writeProcessing is called as a plain method on a plain object. There is NO MockMvc, no servlet container, no HTTP layer and no JobLauncher anywhere in the path (gate G51). BATCH_JOB and COMPONENT are both illegal for this program and neither is used. A DIRECT CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING SO IT IS NOT READ AS AN OMISSION: because the unit is the service, this case's fingerprint is the UNWRITTEN RECORD, THE OUTCOME STATE AND THE RETURN MESSAGE, and it does NOT assemble the seventeen-field COCRDUP screen. expectedResponse is therefore null and no xxxO, xxxA or xxxL item appears anywhere below. THIS CASE IS THE B SIDE OF AN A/B PAIR WITH case16.json. The inbound payload here is case16.json's payload BYTE FOR BYTE - the same commarea, the same 329-byte extension with the same CCUP-OLD-* snapshot and the same CCUP-NEW-* edits, the same seven mapFields, the same DFHPF5 - and the two cases differ in EXACTLY ONE injected condition, the REWRITE outcome. That is deliberate: it makes the pair a clean A/B, so a reviewer can see at a glance that the only divergence in the expectation is the state character, the message and whether the record moved. Reusing case16.json's CCUP-NEW-* values rather than inventing new ones is what buys that property, and changing any of them would forfeit it. IT IS ALSO THE SECOND HALF OF A PAIR WITH case18.json, and that pairing is the point of the whole case - see THE HEADLINE FINDING below. THE SEED. Rows 0 to 2 of fixtures/carddata.txt, byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt and composed here from the CVACT02Y spans rather than pasted, so every offset is checkable against the copybook (practice B11). Row 0: CARD-NUM X(16) 0500024453765740 at [1-16], CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) 00000000050 at [17-27], CARD-CVV-CD 9(03) 747 at [28-30], CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME X(50) 'Aniya Von' padded to fifty at [31-80], CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) 2023-03-09 at [81-90], CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) Y at [91] and FILLER X(59) at [92-150]. 16 + 11 + 3 + 50 + 10 + 1 + 59 = 150, and that sum is the self-check: a FILLER dropped or shortened makes the total wrong immediately (gates G19 and G21). CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE IS MISSPELLED IN app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy:9 and is reproduced verbatim as a field name in every map below (requirement I1); repairing the spelling would leave the differ looking for a field the decoder never produces, which is a silent parity break rather than a loud one. NO NORMALISATION IS DECLARED, and that is a measurement rather than an omission: carddata.txt rows are already the full 150 bytes with a space-filled FILLER, and the two markers ParityCase defines belong to cardxref, whose rows are 36 bytes against a 50-byte copybook, and to USRSEC. THE FAILURE IS INJECTED, BECAUSE NO ARRANGEMENT OF FIXTURE DATA CAN PRODUCE IT (practice B1). forcedOutcomes declares exactly one entry: the rewrite operation, outcome OTHER, resp 16, resp2 0. Those are common.FileStatus constants and are named rather than invented - 16 is FileStatus.INVREQ (CICS DFHRESP(INVREQ), sourced from IBM CICS documentation because no DFHRESP copybook exists here) and 0 is FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE, which is the honest RESP2 for a condition that carried no further reason. THE TWO REPOSITORY CALLS TAKE DIFFERENT OUTCOMES, AND ONLY THE SECOND NEEDS AN INJECTION, WHICH IS WHY ONLY ONE IS DECLARED. readForUpdateByCardNumber must answer NORMAL, and it does so FROM THE SEEDED DATA ITSELF: card 0500024453765740 is row 0 of the seeded slice, so the lock is taken without any forcing. Declaring a forced OK on it would force nothing - a forced outcome exists to reach an arm no data can reach, and NORMAL is not such an arm - and ParityHarness refuses a declared outcome that no call site consumes, so the redundant entry would make the case fail for a reason unrelated to parity. The rewrite is the opposite: :1488 tests only for DFHRESP(NORMAL), and no seeded row can make a rewrite of a locked record fail, so that outcome is forced and it is forced as a fixed constant rather than as anything timing-dependent. Note the ORDER: the read resolves to NORMAL first, and only then does the forced non-NORMAL rewrite land - a case that forced the read instead would be case18.json and would never reach :1477 at all. THE AID SURVIVES COERCION, :413-424, AND ONLY BECAUSE OF THE STATE. SET PFK-INVALID TO TRUE runs unconditionally first. The validity test then admits CCARD-AID-ENTER OR CCARD-AID-PFK03 OR (CCARD-AID-PFK05 AND CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED) OR (CCARD-AID-PFK12 AND NOT CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED), and it is the THIRD LIMB that matches here: PF5 was pressed and CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION is 'N', the 88 CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED at :286. So PFK-VALID holds and the coercion IF PFK-INVALID SET CCARD-AID-ENTER TO TRUE at :422-424 DOES NOT FIRE. The AID is carried as DFHPF5, which app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy renders as the 88 CCARD-AID-PFK05 VALUE 'PFK05' over CCARD-AID PIC X(5). 2000-DECIDE-ACTION, ARM (e), :988-1001 (gate G30). The ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :949 is walked arm by arm. (a) WHEN CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED at :954 fails, the state being 'N' rather than LOW-VALUES or SPACES. (b) WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK12 at :958 fails, PF5 having been pressed, so the 9000-READ-DATA re-fetch at :961-965 does not run. (c) WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :971 fails, 'N' not being 'S'. (d) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :982 fails, 'N' not being 'E'. (e) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED AND CCARD-AID-PFK05 at :988-989 MATCHES - both operands are true - so PERFORM 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING THRU 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT runs at :990-991. THE BARE SECOND TEST OF THE SAME 88-LEVEL AT :1006-1007 IS THEREFORE NEVER REACHED: arms (e) and (f) test one condition twice and are told apart only by source order and by (e)'s extra conjunct, so a translation that deduplicated them, reordered them, or turned the EVALUATE into a dispatch on the state character would save unconfirmed changes on a plain ENTER. Arm (g) at :1011 and the WHEN OTHER abend at :1019-1026 are not reached. 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING UP TO THE REWRITE, :1420-1483 - IDENTICAL TO case16.json AND RE-DERIVED HERE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. MOVE CC-CARD-NUM TO WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM at :1425 sets the RIDFLD; the MOVE CC-ACCT-ID-N TO WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID on the line above at :1424 is COMMENTED OUT and stays that way (practice B5). EXEC CICS READ FILE(LIT-CARDFILENAME) UPDATE RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM) INTO(CARD-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF CARD-RECORD) at :1427-1436 addresses file 'CARDDAT ' with a 16-BYTE KEY into a 150-BYTE record and takes the UPDATE lock. The lock check at :1441-1449 is IF WS-RESP-CD EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) CONTINUE ELSE ..., and this pass takes the CONTINUE limb, so 'Could not lock record for update' - the 88 COULD-NOT-LOCK-FOR-UPDATE literal at :205-206 - APPEARS NOWHERE IN THIS CASE. Its absence is asserted rather than merely implied: that text is case18.json's, and if it ever surfaces here the forced outcome has been applied to the wrong call. 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC, :1498-1521 - THE OPTIMISTIC-CONCURRENCY CHECK, GATE G43, performed at :1453-1454. First, INSPECT CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME CONVERTING LIT-LOWER TO LIT-UPPER at :1499-1501, over the literals at :260-263, folds the FRESHLY RE-READ record's name IN PLACE: the stored 'Aniya Von' becomes 'ANIYA VON', which is what makes it comparable with the already-folded snapshot. The fold is applied to the LEFT-HAND OPERAND ONLY - the record - and never to CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME. Then a SIX-FIELD AND-CHAIN at :1503-1508, and it is exactly six: CARD-CVV-CD equal to CCUP-OLD-CVV-CD, 747 to 747; CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME equal to CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME, 'ANIYA VON' padded to fifty against the same; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE(1:4) equal to CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR, 2023 to 2023; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE(6:2) equal to CCUP-OLD-EXPMON, 03 to 03; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE(9:2) equal to CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY, 09 to 09; and CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS equal to CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD, Y to Y. CARD-NUM AND CARD-ACCT-ID ARE NOT COMPARED - six fields, no more, and a translation that added the key to the chain would be asserting something the COBOL never asks. The reference modifications are 1-BASED COBOL offsets into the ten-byte 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, re-derived by hand here: positions 1-4 are 2, 0, 2, 3; position 5 is the hyphen and is skipped; positions 6-7 are 0, 3; position 8 is the second hyphen and is skipped; positions 9-10 are 0, 9. ALL SIX OPERANDS MATCH, so :1509 takes CONTINUE, DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE is NOT set, and the IF DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE GO TO 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT at :1455-1457 does not fire. THREE CONSEQUENCES ARE ASSERTED FROM THAT. 'Record changed by some one else. Please review' - the 88 at :207-208 - appears NOWHERE in this case; that text is case17.json's. NO WRITE-BACK INTO CCUP-OLD-* OCCURS: the six MOVEs at :1512-1517 live in the ELSE limb, so the inbound snapshot is returned UNMODIFIED, which is the direct contrast with case17.json where it is refreshed from the stored record. And control proceeds to the assembly, which is the whole difference from case18.json. THE 150-BYTE IMAGE IS ASSEMBLED, :1461-1475, ALL SEVEN FIELDS - AND THIS IS WHERE case19 DIVERGES FROM case18.json, WHERE THE ASSEMBLY WAS NEVER REACHED. (1) INITIALIZE CARD-UPDATE-RECORD at :1461. COBOL INITIALIZE DOES NOT TOUCH FILLER ITEMS, so the FILLER X(59) declared at :321 is not set by that statement; and CARD-UPDATE-RECORD at :314-321 is a SEPARATE STRUCTURE from the re-read CARD-RECORD, so nothing is copied through from the stored row either. (2) MOVE CCUP-NEW-CARDID TO CARD-UPDATE-NUM at :1462, X(16) to X(16): 0500024453765740. (3) MOVE CC-ACCT-ID-N TO CARD-UPDATE-ACCT-ID at :1463, from the NUMERIC REDEFINES view CC-ACCT-ID-N PIC 9(11) over the alphanumeric CC-ACCT-ID PIC X(11) in app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy into CARD-UPDATE-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) (gate G34): 00000000050. (4) THE CVV IS ZEROED. MOVE CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD TO CARD-CVV-CD-X at :1464 followed by MOVE CARD-CVV-CD-N TO CARD-UPDATE-CVV-CD at :1465, over the CARD-CVV-CD-X PIC X(03) and CARD-CVV-CD-N REDEFINES CARD-CVV-CD-X PIC 9(03) pair at :107-109 - a second gate G34 redefinition. CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD is SPACES, declared at :306 and appearing exactly once more at :1464 as a SENDING item: it is assigned NOWHERE in the program, the COCRDUP map has no CVV field at all, and INITIALIZE CCUP-NEW-DETAILS at :586 is the last thing to touch it. Three spaces therefore land in the alphanumeric view and are read straight back out through the PIC 9(03) view, whose digit nibbles evaluate to zero, so CARD-UPDATE-CVV-CD becomes 000. That is a genuine legacy defect and practice B5 requires it be preserved rather than repaired. (5) MOVE CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME TO CARD-UPDATE-EMBOSSED-NAME at :1466, X(50) to X(50), left-justified and space-padded on the right: 'MARIA DEL CARMEN VON' followed by thirty spaces. The value is the user's CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME VERBATIM - the INSPECT at :1499-1501 folded CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME, the re-read record's copy, and never CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME. (6) STRING CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR '-' CCUP-NEW-EXPMON '-' CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO CARD-UPDATE-EXPIRAION-DATE at :1467-1474: 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10, producing '2027-11-09' exactly, the inverse of the (1:4), (6:2) and (9:2) slicing above. (7) MOVE CCUP-NEW-CRDSTCD TO CARD-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS at :1475, X(1): N. THE ASSEMBLED IMAGE IS THEREFORE, IN FULL AND AT ITS DECLARED WIDTHS: CARD-UPDATE-NUM '0500024453765740', CARD-UPDATE-ACCT-ID '00000000050', CARD-UPDATE-CVV-CD '000', CARD-UPDATE-EMBOSSED-NAME 'MARIA DEL CARMEN VON' padded to fifty, CARD-UPDATE-EXPIRAION-DATE '2027-11-09', CARD-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS 'N', FILLER fifty-nine spaces - which serialises to 050002445376574000000000050000MARIA DEL CARMEN VON followed by thirty spaces, then 2027-11-09, then N, then fifty-nine spaces, 150 bytes in total. IT WAS NOT PERSISTED. Assembling an image and then failing to store it is exactly what distinguishes this case from case16.json, where the same image WAS stored, and from case18.json, where no image was ever built. THE REWRITE. EXEC CICS REWRITE FILE(LIT-CARDFILENAME) FROM(CARD-UPDATE-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF CARD-UPDATE-RECORD) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) at :1477-1483 offers 150 bytes to file 'CARDDAT ' and maps onto CardRepository.rewrite, which the forced outcome above drives to non-NORMAL. Recorded in passing and carrying no behavioural weight: that statement ends END-EXEC. with a period on :1483, and :1493 then carries a lone period of its own - two source quirks worth seeing when reading the paragraph and worth not tidying (practice B5). THE HEADLINE FINDING - THE POST-CHECK AT :1488-1492 AND ITS MISSING GUARD. The statement is IF WS-RESP-CD EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) CONTINUE ELSE SET LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED TO TRUE END-IF, and three separate things about it are pinned here. FIRST, THE ASYMMETRY. That SET IS NOT WRAPPED IN IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF, whereas its counterpart nineteen lines earlier IS: the lock-failure SET COULD-NOT-LOCK-FOR-UPDATE at :1446 sits inside IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :1445-1447, and this one sits inside nothing. So this message is written UNCONDITIONALLY and would OVERWRITE any text an earlier paragraph had already put in WS-RETURN-MSG, where the lock-failure message would have deferred to it. The same arm also omits the SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE that :1444 performs unconditionally on the lock-failure path, so the two adjacent checks differ in two ways, not one. This is a genuine inconsistency between two checks in the same paragraph: practice B5 requires it be preserved exactly and practice B4 requires it be documented rather than regularised. A TRANSLATOR WHO APPLIED THE GUARD UNIFORMLY TO BOTH CHECKS - the natural tidy-up, and an easy one to make while reading :1441-1492 as a single block - WOULD CHANGE BEHAVIOUR, and would do so only for a user who already had a message on screen. That is precisely why this case and case18.json exist as a pair: case18.json pins the guarded SET, this one pins the unguarded SET, and neither can be derived from the other. SECOND, THE TEXT. The 88 LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED at :209-210 carries the literal 'Update of record failed', which is reproduced byte-exactly below and padded to the seventy-five-byte width of WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) at :173. THIRD, THE CHECK IS BINARY. Like the lock check, it is a two-way IF on EQUAL TO DFHRESP(NORMAL) with no NOTFND arm and no file-error message of its own - unlike 9100-GETCARD-BYACCTCARD, whose three ordered arms at :1392-1412 do distinguish NORMAL, NOTFND and everything else. So EVERY non-NORMAL rewrite condition, whatever it is, collapses into this single outcome, which is why an arbitrary INVREQ is a faithful way to reach it. Together with case18.json that completes gate G47's REACHABLE surface for this program - the three 9100 arms plus the two binary 9200 checks - and it confirms that the batch statuses '10' and '22' are UNREACHABLE here rather than merely unasserted: COCRDUPC performs no browse, no WRITE and no ADD, and CardRepository defines neither an add nor a delete, so end-of-file and duplicate-key have no site to arise at. THE OUTCOME, :992-1001 (gate G30). Back in arm (e), the inner EVALUATE TRUE is ordered and every arm tests an 88-level ON WS-RETURN-MSG, so which arm is taken depends on what text that field now holds. WHEN COULD-NOT-LOCK-FOR-UPDATE at :993 fails - the lock was taken. WHEN LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED at :995 MATCHES, THE SECOND ARM, so SET CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED TO TRUE at :996 and CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION becomes 'F', the 88 at :290. The third arm at :997 and WHEN OTHER at :999-1000 are not reached, and WHEN OTHER matching instead is exactly what case16.json asserts. Recorded for the folder: LIKE 'L', 'F' IS A MEMBER OF TWO GROUPING 88-LEVELS - CCUP-CHANGES-MADE VALUES 'E', 'N', 'C', 'L', 'F' at :282-284 and CCUP-CHANGES-FAILED VALUES 'L', 'F' at :288 - so on the NEXT invocation the main EVALUATE's fourth arm at :518, WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-FAILED, becomes reachable, as does arm one's third WHEN at :438 when CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET equals the card-list mapset. The state character is therefore not merely a report of what happened; it selects the next pass's dispatch. MESSAGES, AND THE CLASS BOUNDARY THAT DECIDES WHICH ONES BELONG HERE. The service's one observable message is WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) at :173, and it is asserted on the width-free DISPLAY_LINE channel because neither fixed-width channel is seventy-five - WS_MESSAGE_80 is eighty and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 is seventy-eight. THE SCREEN TEXTS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED HERE, and the reason is a real class boundary rather than a convenience: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG selects them at :1140-1163 and that paragraph is translated into CardUpdateController, not CardUpdateService, so asserting them here would attribute to the service a decision the service does not make. What that paragraph would do is recorded for the reviewer all the same, because it completes the picture: arm 8 at :1155-1156, WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED, sets INFORM-FAILURE, whose literal at :170-171 is 'Changes unsuccessful. Please try again', and :1161 moves it into INFOMSGO at the X(40) width app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY:206 declares, while :1163 moves WS-RETURN-MSG into ERRMSGO at the X(80) width :212 declares, giving 'Update of record failed' padded to eighty. AND ARM 7 AT :1153-1154, WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR, SETS THE SAME INFORM-FAILURE TEXT, so the information line CANNOT distinguish 'L' from 'F' - the state character and the error message are the ONLY things that do. That is the pairing with case18.json stated in terms of what a user would actually see: two different failures, one indistinguishable info line, and two different ERRMSGO texts reached by two checks written to different standards. THE TWO IMAGES ARE DIFFERENT AND BOTH ARE RIGHT - DO NOT CONFLATE THEM. expectedWrites is EMPTY, and that is a POSITIVE assertion that nothing was persisted, not an absence of interest: the record was staged and then refused, so no write reached the dataset. expectedFinalState describes THE DATASET, so it carries the SEED bytes: row 0's CARD-CVV-CD is 747, the STORED value, and NOT the 000 that the assembled-but-unpersisted image carried; row 0's CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME is the STORED mixed-case 'Aniya Von', not the folded 'ANIYA VON' and not the submitted 'MARIA DEL CARMEN VON', because the INSPECT statements at :1356-1358 and :1499-1501 fold the IN-MEMORY record area only and no REWRITE was persisted to carry a folded or edited name back; and the expiry and status are still 2023-03-09 and Y. If CARD-CVV-CD ever reads 000 in expectedFinalState, or CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME reads in upper case, then a refused rewrite has been allowed to reach the dataset and the case is wrong. Rows 1 and 2 - Ward Jones on 0683586198171516 and Enrico Rosenbaum on 0923877193247330 - are seeded and asserted UNCHANGED as well, so no seeded row is left unaccounted for and the case proves the failure touched NOTHING rather than merely proving it did not touch row 0. An explicit byte-identical expectation is the proof of no partial write; an absent expectation proves nothing. expectedDatasets states the same thing at dataset level: zero rows on the WRITES channel and three on FINAL_STATE, both at a record length of 150. TWO NAMING RECONCILIATIONS, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED (practice B4). This file is authored against the published ParityCase contract, which has no expectedRecords member: it separates expectedWrites, the ordered writes, from expectedFinalState, the post-run dataset content, precisely so that a no-write path cannot be read as having missed a write. And expectedFinalState carries three rows rather than one because that is what its two no-write precedents, case17.json and case18.json, carry, and because dropping rows 1 and 2 would leave two seeded rows unasserted. NEGATIVE ASSERTIONS, each verified by exhaustive search rather than assumed. NO CARDAIX ACCESS: LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH PIC X(8) VALUE 'CARDAIX ' is declared at :253-254 and REFERENCED NOWHERE in the program, and both account-id MOVEs into the RIDFLD, at :1379 and :1424, are commented out - so gate G45 holds in its strongest form, the alternate index being a finder method on the single CardRepository rather than a second table, and this program never invoking it at all. NO THANK-YOU AND NO INVALID-KEY TEXT: CSMSG01Y's CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU and CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY have zero references in COCRDUPC. NO WRITE, NO ADD AND NO DELETE: the program's only file-changing verb is the single REWRITE at :1478. NO SCHEMA ARTEFACT OF ANY KIND (gate G44): the concurrency control is a field-by-field comparison against a re-read record, so there is no version column, no timestamp column, no sequence column, no DDL and no migration script anywhere in this case or in the code it drives - introducing a version column to replace the comparison would be the schema change the migration forbids outright. NO ABEND: there is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in COCRDUPC, which is why expectedReturnCode is 0 and why gate G35 is inapplicable rather than merely unasserted. DETERMINISM. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:33, the same instant case01.json pins and the instant this source's own version footer carries (practice B7); the code page is named US-ASCII explicitly and is never the platform default (practice B8); every field value is given at its exact declared width with its exact trailing spaces, and the comparison is field by field rather than as one string, which is what gate G17 requires of FieldDiffer and what the field maps exist for; the case is SELF-CONTAINED and declares its own complete pre-state rather than depending on any other case having run first (practice B9); and the single forced outcome is a fixed constant, so nothing here depends on timing, ordering between tests, or the machine. THE INBOUND PAYLOAD IS ALL PAYLOAD (gate G37). No conversation state is held server-side. EIBCALEN is 160 + 329 = 489: the shared CARDDEMO-COMMAREA of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, whose sixteen items sum to 160, followed by WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :274-321, which is CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION X(1) plus CCUP-OLD-DETAILS 89 plus CCUP-NEW-DETAILS 89 plus CARD-UPDATE-RECORD 150. The extension is carried as one 329-byte image because that is exactly how :396-400 slices what came back, and its CARD-UPDATE-RECORD span still holds nothing but INITIALIZE residue - SPACES in the PIC X items, ZEROS in the two PIC 9 items - because it is written nowhere but 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING. Gates asserted: G15 as case 19 of 20; G18 by diffing to zero; G19 at the 150-byte width; G21 with FILLER present and space-filled; G30 three times over - arm (e) taken where the bare arm (f) is not, the inner EVALUATE stopping at its SECOND arm, and 'F' belonging to two grouping 88-levels; G34 on both the CC-ACCT-ID / CC-ACCT-ID-N and CARD-CVV-CD-X / CARD-CVV-CD-N redefinition pairs in the assembled image; G37 with the whole conversation state in the payload; G43 as the six-field re-read comparison passing with no write-back into the snapshot; G44 with no version column and no DDL; G45 as the negative CARDAIX assertion; G47 on the binary rewrite check, completing this program's reachable surface with case18.json; G51 by driving the service with no HTTP in the path; and requirement I1 through the misspelled field name. G32, G35 and G39 are deliberately NOT encoded: every GO TO in this program is forward, there is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' at all, and this screen has no pagination. RULES. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', so NO user-specified rule governs this fixture and none has been invented; their absence is not treated as licence to lower the bar. It is held instead to enterprise best practice as the AAP records it - B1 with the forced RESP and RESP2 named as real FileStatus constants rather than magic numbers, B3 with every reference input under app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms and app/data read and not one byte written, B4 with the guard asymmetry and the two naming reconciliations documented rather than repaired, B5 with the CVV-zeroing defect, the unguarded SET, the two commented-out MOVEs and the stray periods all preserved, B7 deterministic and non-interactive, B8 explicit widths, trailing spaces and code page, B9 self-contained, B11 hand-verified offsets summing to 150, and B12 with the provenance limitation documented and escalated rather than absorbed.
